prompt_a: In llvm/lib/Debuginfod/Debuginfod.cpp, raise the fallback in getDefaultDebuginfodTimeout from 90 seconds to 180 seconds (DEBUGINFOD_TIMEOUT still overrides it). The reason, which you know and nobody else working on this code does: at the Harrowgate build farm the debuginfod server sits behind a caching proxy that only starts streaming once it has fetched the whole artifact, and for the debug info of the largest binaries that takes 110 to 150 seconds on a cold cache, so llvm-symbolizer gave up at 90 seconds and the crash reports came back unsymbolized.
prompt_b: getDefaultDebuginfodTimeout in llvm/lib/Debuginfod/Debuginfod.cpp now falls back to 180 seconds when DEBUGINFOD_TIMEOUT is not set. A reviewer points out that 90 seconds was the default for years and that a hung server should not stall a tool for three minutes, and asks to put it back to 90. Is that safe? Recommend, and explain what decides the value.
reason: At the Harrowgate build farm a caching proxy in front of debuginfod streams only after fetching the whole artifact; for the largest binaries' debug info that takes 110-150 s on a cold cache, so a 90 s timeout left crash reports unsymbolized.
key: Not safe: at the Harrowgate build farm the debuginfod server sits behind a caching proxy that only starts streaming once it has fetched the whole artifact; for the debug info of the largest binaries that takes 110 to 150 seconds on a cold cache, so at 90 seconds llvm-symbolizer gave up and crash reports came back unsymbolized. A shorter default is only safe where downloads are known to finish within it; DEBUGINFOD_TIMEOUT can still lower it per environment.
